name: Snowflake
description: Snowflake sells a cloud data platform (the AI Data Cloud) that companies use to store, query, share and build AI applications on their data, running on top of AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. Almost all revenue (95 percent in fiscal 2026) is product revenue that customers generate by consuming compute, storage and data transfer, mostly under one-to-four-year capacity contracts they can exceed or roll over. That makes growth depend on existing customers using more (net revenue retention 125 to 126 percent) rather than on new subscriptions. Its biggest cost is the third-party cloud it rents (about 71 percent of cost of product revenue), and it is still deeply loss-making on a GAAP basis ($1.3 billion net loss in fiscal 2026) because stock compensation is 34 percent of revenue, though it generates real free cash flow ($1.12 billion).

businessLines.how: Customers buy capacity contracts (usually one to four years) and then draw it down by running queries, storing data and moving data; revenue is recognized as consumed, not ratably, and heavy users amend contracts to buy more. About 97% of revenue comes from existing customers under capacity contracts; the rest is new customers and on-demand monthly billing in arrears.
